So in winter 2023-2024, as many of you will know, the Salvation Army Prairie Harm Reduction and St. Mary's Parish Saskatoon.
We're together to provide overnight warming center options.
St. Mary's emergency overnight warming center, operating from a temporary location, provided a warm location for an average of 122 individuals per night last winter.
During extreme cold weather events, the numbers surge to 230 people.

With continued increases in the number of people experiencing homelessness in our community, community partners in Saskatoon have been working together and have identified the need for additional facilities and outreach support for this winter.
This will help us to ensure the safety and well-being of those residents experiencing homelessness.
Although planning for this work began in the spring of 2024, it was exceptionally difficult to find and secure locations for this winter.
There were a few reasons for that. Many community partners and locations were considered that there were very few facilities of sufficient size and setup that were available.
Many community partners who considered providing a location indicated that they already have challenges meeting their core services.
Due to demand and they couldn't risk expanding services to include the warming center.

Due to the hours of operations required a number of potentially suitable locations were also not available because many facilities already had programming for various events and activities that would have to be relocated or canceled to use their location.
Multiple organizations and individuals assisted in trying to find locations for this winter.
And through a multi-party collaborative process, two locations have now been secured and expanded outreach capacity has been identified.

This year's plan includes an evening warming location and an overnight warming location for women to be operated at the Saskatoon Indian Amate Friendship Center and an overnight warming location for men operated by the Salvation Army at St. Mary's Parish.
Expanded outreach service will be provided by Swaya Toten outreach from the Saskatoon Tribal Council.

Administration and other community partners will also continue to assist both of these facilities to be able to address their particular needs as a result of the use of their facilities for warming centers.
However, for these facilities and services to be operational this year, full funding is required.
This has been estimated by the partners to get total of $1.2 million dollars.

Multiple funding partners have already been confirmed, including the problems of Saskatoon, the Government of Canada reaching home funding administered by the Saskatoon Housing Initiative's partnership and a number of private and agency donors which are noted in the report.
We are extremely thankful for these contributions and for all the work that all of the partners have done to get us to secured facilities.
The donations and the funding that we have to date combined comes to $1 million dollars.
So that does leave us with a gap and we need to fill that gap in order to ensure we can have the full funding to secure the locations and the staffing for the entire period of time.
So we are requesting a $200,000 contribution from the city of Saskatoon to fill that funding gap and the recommended funding source for this at this time is the reserve for capital expenditures.
